page.text:
While equivalence relations formalize symmetry and clustering, *order
relations* formalize comparison, ranking, and hierarchy.

A *partial order* is reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive. It allows
incomparable elements: two elements $x, y$ may satisfy neither $x \le y$
nor $y \le x$ (as in subset inclusion $\mathcal{P}(U)$ or divisibility in
$\mathbb{N}$). A *total order* (or linear order) is a partial order in
which every pair of elements is comparable ($x \le y \lor y \le x$),
eliminating all ambiguity of precedence.
